correctness.rationale: Cauchy–Binet gives the sum of squared pair sines. Write theta=t·1+z with sum z=0; then the sum of squared pair differences is m||z||². On the folded interval, |sin u|≥2|u|/π, and the larger Gram eigenvalue is at most m, so the small-eigenvalue event is globally confined to ||z||≤πε/2. Near that diagonal the determinant is m||z||²+O(||z||⁴) and the larger eigenvalue is m+O(||z||²), giving the claimed transverse unit ball. The Jacobian is sqrt(m); after rescaling, dominated convergence applies for every interior t even if f vanishes, and endpoints have zero longitudinal measure. In the uniform m=2 case λ=1−cos|θ1−θ2|, and triangular integration gives leading coefficient 2sqrt(2)/L, an exact normalization check. Strict Jensen gives the unique continuous minimizer. Integrating the positive tail coefficient gives the strict inverse-moment cutoff for s>0, including divergence at equality; conditional OLS risk is σ² times the sum of the two inverse eigenvalues, so it is finite exactly for m≥4. The iid pair expectation follows from the double-angle cosine; zero mean of e^(2it) forces support on the endpoints by its positive interior imaginary part, and then equal masses. The singular probability is the probability all endpoint draws agree.

value.rationale: The smallest eigenvalue controls noise amplification in this minimal support-reconstruction model. Its exact design-dependent tail distinguishes rank almost surely from finite mean-square error and singles out a continuous optimum. The contrast with the D-optimal design, which creates a positive singular mass, is substantive and interpretable even though the expected-determinant calculation alone is elementary.
residual_risks: No conclusion about risk of constrained procedures, unknown orientations, or design optimality for other losses.
